title: Manufacture of nitric acid by Ostwald's process
topicTitle: Manufacture of nitric acid by Ostwald's process
notes: Ostwald's process makes nitric acid from ammonia, air, and water.
Catalytic oxidation: 4NH3 + 5O2 → 4NO + 6H2O. A platinum-rhodium gauze is used at about 800–900°C. The reaction is exothermic, so once it is started the heat of reaction keeps the gauze hot.
The nitric oxide is cooled and oxidised further: 2NO + O2 → 2NO2.
Absorption in water gives nitric acid: 4NO2 + O2 + 2H2O → 4HNO3. Nitrogen monoxide formed in a side absorption step is returned for further oxidation.
Excess air supplies the oxygen for both oxidations. The catalyst is required because the uncatalysed oxidation of ammonia is too slow to be useful in the plant.
